rows.verified: DSEAR requires employers to control safety risks from fire, explosion and substances corrosive to metals.
DSEAR duties protect employees and members of the public who may be put at risk by work activity.
Employers must identify dangerous substances present in the workplace and assess the associated risks.
Risks must be removed where possible or controlled with suitable measures where removal is not possible.
Controls must be provided to reduce the effects of incidents involving dangerous substances.
Plans and procedures are required for accidents, incidents and emergencies involving dangerous substances.
Employees must be properly informed and trained to control or deal with dangerous-substance risks.
Areas where explosive atmospheres may occur must be identified and classified, with ignition sources avoided in those areas.
DSEAR controls depend on substance inventory, physical state, concentration, ventilation, containment, ignition sources, process conditions and emergency arrangements.
DSEAR evidence is substance-, process-, inventory- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.
Employers must protect employees and other people affected by their work from slip and trip risks so far as reasonably practicable.
Slip and trip risks must be assessed and action taken where necessary.
Workplace floors must be suitable, in good condition and free from obstructions so people can move safely.
Water, oil, ice and other contamination can create slipping hazards.
Pallets, uneven ground, strapping and trailing cables are examples of tripping hazards that should be controlled.
Rain, puddles, mud, ice and poor lighting can increase slip and trip risks in outdoor areas.
Liquid spillages should be cleaned promptly, the area dried and suitable warning signs used.
Workers should report near misses, accidents and dangerous slip or trip conditions promptly.
Slip-and-trip controls depend on flooring, contamination, drainage, housekeeping, footwear, lighting, weather, traffic and maintenance.
Slip-and-trip evidence is route-, surface-, activity- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
